claim: Crosswalk (guest commentary by Amber Ginter, 2026-10-08) reports a 70-person Nashville team led by 28-year-old Micah Fiechter is using AI to set the whole Bible to music.
quote: a team of 70 people in Nashville, Tenn., is on a mission to use the technology to convert the entire Bible into musical form. What started as a passion project by 28-year-old Micah Fiechter to turn a single Bible chapter into music for his father's sermon

claim: The project began with 1 John 4 for Fiechter's father's sermon.
quote: "Dad asked if I could work on 1 John 4 , and it sort of just went from there," Fiechter explained.

claim: Per Fiechter, the whole Bible is available in 11 styles in the Music Bible app, with more than 30,000 songs and three Spanish genres (as of the Crosswalk piece).
quote: Fiechter stated that anyone can now listen to the entire Bible in 11 styles using his app, Music Bible.

claim: Crosswalk gives the song count as more than 30,000 and quotes the app's 'first complete, unedited' description.
quote: the app has more than 30,000 songs and is described as "the world's first complete, unedited, verse-by-verse Bible in song app." The app currently features three genres in Spanish

claim: Fiechter's stated philosophy: music is changed to fit Scripture, not the reverse.
quote: We don't change Scripture to fit music; we change music to fit Scripture.

claim: Fiechter on the goal of pointing to the Bible rather than the product.
quote: I don't want people to remember Music Bible; I want them to remember the Bible.

claim: The Music Bible app is free on iOS and Android.
quote: The Music Bible app can be downloaded for free on iOS and Android.

claim: Music Bible says it uses Suno and ChatGPT to help create arrangements, instrumentals and vocals.
quote: The Music Bible® utilizes AI platforms including Suno and ChatGPT to assist in creating musical arrangements, instrumentals, and vocals.

claim: Music Bible pledges never to use AI to interpret, paraphrase or extrapolate Scripture.
quote: The Music Bible® will never use artificial intelligence to create songs that interpret, paraphrase, or extrapolate the meaning of Scripture.

claim: Music Bible says verses are not reordered, repeated or rearranged and there are no choruses, but allows occasional word/phrase repetition.
quote: The verses are not taken out of order, not repeated, and not rearranged. The song begins with the first word and ends with the final word of the referenced passage; occasionally, a word or phrase may be repeated for musical expression. There are no choruses or lyrical additions

claim: Music Bible justifies AI by the scale of the task (over 750,000 words).
quote: the practical scope of setting the entire Bible, over 750,000 words, to music has as of 2025 exceeded what any single artist or team could accomplish.

claim: Music Bible's stated accuracy commitment is worded as 'at least 100% accuracy'; no error rate or review method is published on the page.
quote: Maintaining at least 100% accuracy in the oral representation of each passage.

claim: Music Bible describes itself as organizers of a new medium, not artists, and hopes human artists will perform word-for-word Scripture Songs.
quote: We are not artists or musicians but instead organizers of a new medium to experience the Scriptures in their unedited form.

claim: Music Bible's site says it reaches 136 countries and is free on every platform; it also links to a YouVersion listening page.
quote: Bringing God's Word to life through song, now reaching 136 countries.

claim: Music Bible homepage counters (in page HTML) show 38,556 Scripture songs, 14 complete-Bible genres, 136 countries and a 5.7 (billion) 'People Reached by 2028' goal. Labels: Scripture Songs / Complete Bible Genres / Countries / People Reached by 2028.
quote: data-to-value="38556" ... data-to-value="14" ... data-to-value="136" ... data-to-value="5.7"

claim: Music Bible claims two-thirds of the world learns by listening (company claim, not independently verified here).
quote: Two-thirds of the world learns by listening. This was built for them, and for everyone else too.

claim: Music Bible's app offers AI-generated playlists from text prompts, plus read-along lyrics and a Bible-in-one-year path.
quote: Describe the kind of playlist you want and AI will create it for you.

claim: Fiechter's Washington Examiner op-ed (2026-10-11) is headlined around 38,000 AI songs and a Gutenberg comparison; body is paywalled.
quote: How 38,000 AI songs might be the biggest shift in Bible access since Gutenberg By Micah Fiechter Published October 11, 2026 11:00am ET

claim: The op-ed's summary argues strict boundaries make AI safe for Scripture-in-song.
quote: AI poses real dangers, but strict boundaries allow us to safely harness the technology to make Scripture accessible through music.

claim: TheSinging.Bible facts page (as of 2026-10-04): 22 styles (20 English, 2 Spanish), 44 versions per chapter, 52,316 recordings, all 1,189 chapters.
quote: Sung chapters 52,316 recordings: 47,560 in English and 4,756 in Spanish

claim: TheSinging.Bible's English text is the Singing Bible Edition based on the Berean Standard Bible; Spanish is Reina-Valera 1909.
quote: English The Singing Bible Edition (SBE), based on the Berean Standard Bible (BSB) Spanish Reina-Valera 1909

claim: TheSinging.Bible says recordings follow the written text, which is shown, and were produced with AI-empowered technologies.
quote: How it is sung Word for word: every recording follows the written text, which is shown with every chapter How it is made The renditions were produced with AI-empowered technologies

claim: TheSinging.Bible is free with no sign-up or ads; iOS app since 2026-09-21, Android since 2026-10-04, 24/7 YouTube radio since 2026-10-02.
quote: Website thesinging.bible : free, no sign-up, no ads iPhone and iPad App Store , since September 21, 2026 Android Google Play , since October 4, 2026 TheSinging.Bible Radio Live on YouTube around the clock, since October 2, 2026

claim: TheSinging.Bible, LLC is based in Colorado Springs and launched 2026-08-25.
quote: Organization TheSinging.Bible, LLC, Colorado Springs, Colorado, USA Launched August 25, 2026

claim: The collection totals about 4,500 hours; the site frames it as 22 styles x 2 voices x 1,189 chapters.
quote: The collection holds 52,316 chapter recordings — 22 musical styles × 2 voices × all 1,189 chapters of the Bible.

claim: Fun fact: Jonah is available as a sea shanty; genealogies are sung too.
quote: Jonah is available as a sea shanty. A sailor's story, finally in sailors' music.

claim: Under 20 minutes a day covers the whole Bible in a year; text can be displayed while playing.
quote: Under 20 minutes of listening a day sings you through the entire Bible in one year.

claim: Answered Faith: TheSinging.Bible launched Aug 25 with 38,048 recordings across all 1,189 chapters.
quote: TheSinging.Bible launched August 25 with 38,048 recordings spanning all 1,189 chapters of Scripture.

claim: The one-million-plays and 194-countries figures are self-reported and unaudited; plays are not unique listeners.
quote: The one-million-play figure and reported reach into 194 countries come from the project's own analytics. They have not been independently audited, and a play should not be confused with a unique listener or a completed chapter.

claim: Ron Forseth is founder and executive producer of TheSinging.Bible.
quote: The site's founder and executive producer, Ron Forseth, said the goal was simple: allow people to experience all of the Bible through different kinds of music.

claim: A team of 20+ used AI tools; the project says humans managed and reviewed the recordings.
quote: The enormous library was created by a team of more than 20 people using a collection of modern artificial-intelligence tools. The project says producers, engineers, quality-control reviewers, managers and digital specialists remained responsible for managing and reviewing the recordings.

claim: The release did not name all tools, explain synthetic voices, or publish error rates.
quote: The release does not identify all the tools used, explain how synthetic voices were generated or publish detailed error rates from its quality-control process.

claim: Risks named: mispronunciation, odd emphasis, mood clashing with lament or the Passion.
quote: Artificial intelligence can mispronounce names, place emphasis in strange locations or produce a musical mood that fights against a passage's meaning.

claim: Melody is interpretive even when lyrics are exact; a performance is not new biblical authority.
quote: Pastors should also make clear that a musical performance is not a new form of biblical authority. Melody involves interpretation.

claim: Plays cannot measure spiritual engagement.
quote: Plays, impressions and shares may show reach, but they cannot measure repentance, understanding, obedience or growing love for Christ.

claim: Bibles For The World (Colorado Springs) was an early supporter of TheSinging.Bible.
quote: Bibles For The World, a Colorado Springs ministry, was an early supporter of the project.

claim: The BSB is public domain (since 2023-04-30) and asks that derivatives that vary from the official text not use the Berean name; this context bears on why the sung text is called the 'Singing Bible Edition'. Whether/how SBE differs from BSB is unverified.
quote: For derivative works that vary from the official text, we respectfully request that the Berean name is not used.

claim: BSB public-domain dedication date.
quote: The Berean Bible and Majority Bible texts are officially dedicated to the public domain as of April 30, 2023.

claim: Barna (2026-10-06): 33% of U.S. Protestant pastors feel positive about AI writing worship songs; 29% about AI interpreting scripture; 64% about AI creating curriculum.
quote: They are most positive about AI creating programs such as curriculum for small groups or Bible studies (64%). Far fewer feel positive about AI writing prayers (37%) or worship songs (33%), interpreting scripture (29%) or writing a sermon (27%).

claim: Barna: 94% of pastors say churches should have AI guidelines; only 4% have a formal policy and 17% informal guidance.
quote: In practice, only 4 percent of pastors say their own church has a formal policy, and 17 percent say it has informal guidance. The other 79 percent have neither.

claim: Barna pastor survey method: n=442, online, December 2025, +/-2.8%.
quote: The U.S. Protestant pastors survey ( n =442) was conducted online in December 2025, using representative quotas for church size, denomination, and region.

claim: Barna (2026-08-25): 94% of pastors, 83% of practicing Christians and 74% of U.S. adults are concerned about AI misinterpreting scripture.
quote: Nearly three-quarters of U.S. adults (74%) say they are concerned about AI misinterpreting scripture. Among practicing Christians, that figure rises to 83 percent, and among pastors, 94 percent.

claim: Worship leader Derek Volkmann (Worship Strategies, 2026-02-21) voiced unease about AI-made Scripture songs, citing YouVersion's Bible in a Year Through Song (explicitly as observation, not confirmed).
quote: To be clear, this is observational, not a confirmed claim about the production process.

claim: Volkmann's core objection: words are true but the AI rendering does not feel true; he will promote human alternatives.
quote: Even though the words are true, it doesn't necessarily feel true.

claim: Volkmann does not tell people to stop listening, but will promote the human alternative.
quote: I don't think I would stop anyone from listening to things like Bible in a Year Through Music —but you better believe that I'll always promote the human alternative.

claim: Baptist worship pastor Kevin Uhrich (via Religion Unplugged/Baptist Press, 2026-01-03) accepts AI in production but draws the line at the words.
quote: However, I personally believe we need to draw the line when it comes to the words written on the page. That must remain the work of a human.

claim: Kenny Lamm (NC Baptists) urges discernment over blanket fear: AI may assist the craft but not replace human worshippers.
quote: the church holds a hard line that AI can assist the craft but cannot replace the heart and witness of human worshippers

claim: Keith Getty (Christian Post, 2026-08-20) frames 'singing the Bible' as central in the AI age.
quote: There are many goals with the Sing! Conference: congregational singing, to improve high artistry, but I think at the heart of it is helping people sing the Bible

claim: Deseret News (via KSL, 2026-06-01): Come and See uses an AI tool for a first-pass translation of The Chosen in minority languages, followed by expert review; majority languages use conventional dubbing without AI.
quote: Come and See uses the AI-based app to generate a first pass of the translation, followed by a meticulous review from subject matter experts to ensure quality and accuracy.

claim: Goal: all seven seasons in 600 languages; 500+ are minority languages without dubbing infrastructure.
quote: Of the languages slated for translation, more than 500 are minority languages with no existing dubbing infrastructure

claim: Speech-to-speech AI overlays the original actor's voice onto linguists' recordings.
quote: speech-to-speech AI technology is then used to overlay the sound of the original voice actor onto the audio provided by linguists and translators.

claim: Movieguide (2026-10-13) re-reports the Chosen AI workflow, citing Deseret News and China Christian Daily interviews and a Come and See fact sheet. Quote extracted via a fetch tool (page blocks direct download); treat wording as near-verbatim.
quote: a trained subject matter expert examines each line for accuracy, biblical fidelity and cultural relevance.

claim: Gloo's fourth annual AI hackathon (Boulder, Oct 6-8, 2026) drew 1,000+ participants on 115+ teams from 12 countries.
quote: Leading technology platform Gloo held its fourth annual hackathon this year in Boulder, Colorado, from Oct. 6-8. Over 1,000 people competed in person and remotely on more than 115 teams, representing 12 countries, 34 states, and eight universities.

claim: Biola team Holy Sound reached the finals with a natural-language controller for church sound (Ableton Live).
quote: Biola University's team Holy Sound made it to the finals for their solution that allows people to use natural language to run sound boards. It is specifically designed to help non-technical people use Ableton Live during church services.

claim: Austin Christian University's Fosterly won the $100,000 grand prize; Unify, Envoy and Frontier Commons won $20,000 track prizes (Agents, Bible, Ministry Resourcing).
quote: Austin Christian University 's Fosterly won the $100,000 grand prize for helping young adults who have aged out of foster care. Teams Unify, Envoy, and Frontier Commons each won $20,000 in the Agents, Bible, and Ministry Resourcing tracks, respectively.
